objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (19 November 2026) on CREATED-PAIR-20261119-001's direction 1. Carried meet-once collisions stay together a round further and the created one parts; the difference is whether a table isometry keeps the growing end. State exactly what one complete round reads of an arrangement, and prove or refute: an isometry of bond-distance tables that keeps it extends to an isometry of the next round's tables. Check on GROW-SMALL's 86 carried pairs and PARENT-RULE's static pairs; say what the 6 small pairs failing CREATED-PAIR's growing-end test are. If true, it is the clean form of the owner's premise that distance plus the growing end carries what grows. Serves A97, A108 and G1.
status: Complete 2026-11-19 (Partial; referee pending): one round reads only the live junctions, their loose counts and the sets of them met by one junction (Lemma A, proved); with equations it gives persistence forever (Claim B*, proved); with the table in place of the equations (Claim B), all 2,198 tested extensions on 57 reached carried pairs are isometries of the next tables, but no proof; persistence without the reading is common (the 6, 43 static pairs).
stop_rule: A proof that the extension is an isometry, or a counterexample (a pair with an isometry keeping what the round reads whose next tables are not isometric); referee hand-off; report.
title: Does a table isometry that keeps what the round reads extend one round?
